summary: The flat top-level frame a STRATEGY_STATUS push carries end to end. Producing side: backend_app/backend/strategy_service.py's deploy_strategy (running/failed) and stop_deployment (stopped), each calling app_state.ws.broadcast_user(user_id, frame). Consuming side: algo22-terminal/src/websocketClient.js's wsClient.subscribeStrategyStatus, which subscribes to the exact event-type key 'STRATEGY_STATUS' (websocketClient.js:1202-1205), routed through processMessage's exact match on message.type. Read by algo22-terminal/src/design/pageFields.js's 'deploymentStopped' declaration (read: wsClient.subscribe('STRATEGY_STATUS'), path: 'status') and rendered by pages/LiveTrading.jsx.
one_file_note: This file is the single copy. pytest (tests/test_strategy_status_publish.py) reads it directly at tests/fixtures/strategy_status_frame.json; vitest (algo22-terminal/tests/unit/liveTrading/deploymentState.test.jsx) reads the same path through node:fs, repo-relative. A per-side copy could drift on the one thing that matters most here - the exact spelling of `type` - which is precisely the three-way mismatch 1.24 names (no publisher, the wrong envelope on the only broadcaster that exists, and the subscriber's upper-case spelling). Declaring `type` once, read by both sides, is what makes that mismatch impossible to reintroduce silently.

producer.note: The frame passed to broadcast_user is not wrapped. ws_manager.py's _broadcast does json.dumps(data) and ws.send_text(...) directly on what broadcast_user is given, so the dict below is the literal top-level JSON the browser receives - never a `{"type": "dashboard_update", ...}` envelope. broadcast_dashboard_update (api_ws/ws_routes.py) is NOT used for this: it wraps every frame it is given as `{"type": "dashboard_update", "update_type": ...}`, which is a different, wrongly-enveloped frame this fixture's second example exists to name and rule out.

type.note: Upper case, exactly. websocketClient.js's processMessage routes on an exact match of message.type against the event-type key a subscriber registered with (websocketClient.js:571-582); wsClient.subscribeStrategyStatus registers 'STRATEGY_STATUS' (websocketClient.js:1202-1205). A lower-case or wrapped type is silently dropped, not coerced.

strategy_id.note: liveFrame.js's isFreshFrame does not gate on this field itself; algo22-terminal/src/pages/LiveTrading.jsx compares it against the strategy the tier-1 leaf is showing before accepting the frame's `status`.

status.from: the same literal strategy_service.py writes to strategy_deployments.status/strategies.status in the same call
status.note: The only field pageFields.js's 'deploymentStopped' entry declares a path for (path: 'status'). deploymentState.test.jsx's existing cases also push 'error' and 'disconnected' as worker-run-state values the frontend already handles; this backend publish emits only the three values a deploy/stop transition actually produces today.

environment.from: deploy_strategy's environment parameter / the deployment row's environment column
environment.note: Optional. components/trading/liveFrame.js's isFreshFrame treats an absent environment as passing every ledger's gate (a frame naming no ledger is not evidence against any of them); a frame naming one is declined by a panel on a different or unconfirmed ledger. Included here because both publish call sites have it on hand at zero extra cost, and omitting it on a live-vs-paper mismatch is the exact confusion Requirement 14.5 exists to prevent.

error.from: the fleet call's failure message (deploy_strategy's `message` on the failed branch)
error.note: Present only on status: "failed". deploymentState.test.jsx's existing 'error' case already renders this verbatim as the worker's own reason (task 20.5); this publish supplies it on the one transition that has a message to give - a failed deploy attempt. stop_deployment's stop never sets this field.

not_included.timestamp: Read nowhere. pageFields.js declares only `path: 'status'` for this field and no consumer in algo22-terminal reads a time off a STRATEGY_STATUS frame - unlike the unrelated ccxt order `timestamp` in pages/LiveTrading.jsx, which is a different fact. Adding an unread field here would be exactly what this fixture's own convention (tests/fixtures/backtest_payload_keys.json's producer note) warns against: a key present because it seemed natural, not because a reader consumes it.

example.note: One successful start. `strategy_id` and `status` are what the frontend's declared `path` reads; `environment` demonstrates the ledger-gate field being populated from the same call.

wrong_envelope_example.note: What broadcast_dashboard_update would have produced had 8.5 routed through it instead - task 8.4/8.6's explicit negative case. websocketClient.js's processMessage matches message.type exactly against 'STRATEGY_STATUS'; this object's type is 'dashboard_update', so no STRATEGY_STATUS subscriber is ever called for it. This is the shape tests/test_strategy_status_publish.py and deploymentState.test.jsx both assert must NOT be treated as a strategy status update.
